solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Policy position example not popular at first

indicators.note: not says a word is to be left out of what precedes
the dropped word must come off the front, the place a first part sits

blocks.note: an instance is an example
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: A political stance is illustrated by an example that was unpopular at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove IN from the start of INSTANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is the attitude or line a person or party takes on an issue, a synonym for a policy position.

clue.text: Ray's small jab

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
to poke is to jab

explanation.surface: Someone called Ray throws a little jab.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray looks like a boxer's name, but it is the definition: a ray is a line radiating from a centre, like a wheel's spoke.
explanation.definitionFit: The radiating rods of a wheel are spokes, and a ray is any line radiating from a hub.

clue.text: Company broadcast row

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
a line is a row

explanation.surface: A firm gets into a public argument that is broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Row suggests a quarrel, but it means a line of things.
explanation.definitionFit: An airline is a business operating flights, so it is a kind of company.

clue.text: Grasping anger finally, unexpectedly concedes noise at its peak

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the preceding word
something happening unexpectedly comes out in a surprising form, so the letters are rearranged
to grasp is to hold within, so one part closes around the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the final letter of anger

explanation.surface: Someone yields to growing anger as the din rises to a climax.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange CONCEDES as CESCENDO and slip R in after the first C.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescendo is the climax of a gradual increase in volume, the loudest point of the sound.

clue.text: Rest of snooker player's team absorbing pressure? Right

indicators.note: something absorbing a thing takes it inside itself

blocks.note: a side is a team
P is the symbol for pressure
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: The rest of a snooker player's team seems to be taking the strain, and rightly.
explanation.walkthrough: Rest is not the remainder but the cue rest; in snooker a spider is a rest with a raised head for bridging over balls.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker, a spider is a cue rest with tall legs used to reach over intervening balls.

clue.text: From time to time pained, try devotion?

indicators.note: from time to time means occasionally, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether occasionally trying while in pain counts as devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety is religious devoutness, reverence shown to God through worship.

clue.text: Academic accepting old record and greeting swimmer

indicators.note: one who accepts something takes it in, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a don is a university teacher
an LP is a long-playing vinyl record, an old format
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A lecturer takes an old record and says hello to someone swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a British university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge; 'old' qualifies the record rather than giving O.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolphin is a marine mammal famed for swimming, so it is aptly called a swimmer.

clue.text: Tough, having to take exam again — about right!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: to resit is to take an exam again
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: It is tough to have to retake an exam, and that is fair enough.
explanation.walkthrough: A lien is the legal right to keep someone's property until they pay what they owe.
explanation.definitionFit: Resilient means hardy and able to recover from setbacks, the sense of tough as durable.

clue.text: Good time for tea? Not at first, but came across foodie

indicators.note: not at first says the opening letter is missing

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
four o'clock is the traditional teatime
to meet is to come across

explanation.surface: A food lover turns up at tea, though not at the start of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Afternoon tea is traditionally at four o'clock; drop its F.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmet is a connoisseur of good food, which is what a foodie is too.

clue.text: Madrid team first — I'm not making it up!

blocks.note: Real Madrid is the Spanish football club
1st written with I for the figure one

explanation.surface: A football fan insists that Real Madrid top the table, honestly.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist deals in facts rather than fantasy, so might say of their claims that nothing is invented.

clue.text: Not agreeing, Democrat insisted changes needed

indicators.note: when something changes it takes a new form, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A Democrat who disagrees insists that changes are required.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissident opinion is one that departs from the official line, that is, dissenting.

clue.text: CEO, timid, extremely ropy, maybe this?

definitions.text: CEO, timid, extremely ropy, maybe this?

indicators.note: extremely points to the outermost letters, the extremes of the word
maybe hints at a possible version, so the letters may be arranged otherwise

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of ropy

explanation.surface: A boss who is timid and thoroughly poor might be the very picture of second-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a timid, ropy chief executive is an example of it. Ropy is British slang for poor quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediocrity is the state of being only ordinary or second-rate, and a weak CEO exemplifies it.

clue.text: Hear about latest offer — first of all ring

indicators.note: first of all asks for the opening letter of each word in turn

blocks.note: the initial letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Someone is told to listen to news of a new deal before ringing.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes the first four words read as news to hear, but their initials supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is a circle of light around a saint's head or the moon, so it is a ring.

clue.text: Back settled in Ulster now

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone has come back and settled in Northern Ireland for good.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is the northern province of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rear part of a ship, its back end.

clue.text: One's a fall guy as a pact goes awry

indicators.note: when things go awry they go wrong and out of order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: When a deal collapses, somebody ends up carrying the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: The word goes is part of the fodder as well as the indicator: rearrange A PACT GOES.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapegoat is someone made to take the blame for others, which is a fall guy in idiom.

clue.text: Short time, I hesitate to say, for one providing support

blocks.note: a second is a short span of time
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone pauses awkwardly for a moment before admitting they will back a proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: A seconder formally supports a motion in a meeting after it has been proposed.

clue.text: Accountant's part bringing in southeastern dish

indicators.note: bringing in means taking something inside, so it sits within

blocks.note: CA is chartered accountant, plus the possessive S
SE is the abbreviation for southeastern
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: An accountant's role involves introducing a dish from the southeast.
explanation.walkthrough: CA stands for chartered accountant, the British professional qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole is a stew slowly cooked in the oven, served as a dish, and named after its pot.

clue.text: Dad's blade that may help to gain entry

definitions.text: that may help to gain entry

blocks.note: pa is dad, plus the possessive S
a sword is a blade

explanation.surface: Father's sword might be used to force a way inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as part of a description of the blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A password is a secret word that grants access to a computer or guarded place.

clue.text: Politician, guy from Spain, welcoming a Tory's introduction

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the following letters go inside
an introduction comes at the start, so the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: señor is Spanish for a man
taken as written
the first letter of Tory

explanation.surface: A Spanish politician welcomes a Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, an elected or appointed politician.

clue.text: Very little in way — that's gratifying

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: wee is Scottish for small
ST is street, a way

explanation.surface: Something small but pleasing happens, and it is satisfying.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet in the sense of pleasing or delightful, as in sweet success, is a synonym for gratifying.

clue.text: Important place, oligarch's content to leave to be rebuilt

indicators.note: if the inside letters depart only the two ends remain
rebuilding puts the same parts together in a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of oligarch

explanation.surface: A tycoon is happy to let an important building be redeveloped.
explanation.walkthrough: Content looks like happy, but it means the inside of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Epochal means significant enough to mark an epoch, a momentous or important event.

clue.text: Incline to be short of fat

blocks.note: first meaning: to tilt or slope
second meaning: of meat, without much fat

explanation.surface: Someone tends towards being slim.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for slanting or tilting, and an adjective for meat or bodies having little fat.

clue.text: From now on fellow attending Northern church by river

blocks.note: he refers to a male fellow
N is the abbreviation for northern
CE is the Church of England
the Forth is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: From today a man will go to a northern church beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Henceforth is a formal adverb meaning from this time onwards.

clue.text: Large group in store, they say

indicators.note: they say points to how a word is spoken rather than written

blocks.note: a hoard is a stored stockpile

explanation.surface: A big crowd is in a shop, so people report.
explanation.walkthrough: Store looks like a shop but is a stockpile.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large crowd or throng of people.

clue.text: Delay attempt to admit artist on the rise

indicators.note: admitting someone lets them in, so the next part goes inside
in a down clue rising means reading upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: a try is an attempt
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A rising artist is held back by an attempt to get them accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is to linger or dawdle, so to be slow in going, which is to delay.

clue.text: Large water creature ultimately slippery that's hard to predict

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large
an otter is an aquatic mammal
the last letter of slippery

explanation.surface: A big aquatic animal is ultimately slippery and impossible to forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery is any matter of pure chance, so its outcome cannot be foreseen.

clue.text: Place of obscurity new hero could emerge from?

definitions.text: Place of obscurity new hero could emerge from?

indicators.note: something emerging from material is made out of it in a new form

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An unknown hero could come out of obscurity, as new stars often do.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a new hero often seems to come from nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowhere means a state of obscurity, as in coming from nowhere to fame.

clue.text: After despicable person rebuffed, understand objective

indicators.note: something rebuffed is pushed back, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: a rat is a despicable person
to get something is to understand it

explanation.surface: Once a nasty person is rejected, you can grasp the goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A target is an aim or goal, which is what an objective is.

clue.text: Shout back briefly after sea race

indicators.note: back means read in the opposite direction
briefly says the word is cut short by a letter

blocks.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
to yell is to shout

explanation.surface: A swimmer shouts back quickly after a race at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A medley is a swimming race in which each length or leg uses a different stroke.
